title: V-Stitch Triangle Shawl
subtitle: Top-down triangle with a classic 2tr-ch1-2tr V-stitch pattern in DK weight
excerpt: A top-down triangular shawl built entirely from V-stitches: each V is 2 trebles with a chain-1 space between them, worked into the chain space of the V below. DK weight on a 4mm hook produces light, drapey fabric with a consistent open mesh.
sourceNotes: Original pattern synthesised for Homemade. V-stitch construction is a well-established technique with no single source.
heroPrompt: A triangular crochet shawl in soft teal DK yarn showing a regular open V-stitch mesh. Top edge draped over a rustic wooden coat hook, point hanging free. Soft window light.

glossaryTerms.definition: Two trebles with a chain between them, all worked into the same space. Creates an open, lacy fabric.
The gap created by one or more skipped chains. The hook enters the space beneath the chain, not through a stitch top.

content.text: This shawl is a top-down triangle measuring approximately 150cm across the top edge and 75cm from the top to the lower point. You begin with a short foundation chain at the centre top and work outward, adding one V-stitch at each edge on every row. A V-stitch is two trebles with a chain-1 space between them, worked into the chain space of the V-stitch below. Because every V sits over the previous V, the pattern is self-correcting: if you can see where the last V sat, you know exactly where to place the next one. DK weight yarn on a 4mm hook produces a light, open fabric that drapes well as a shoulder wrap or evening layer.

Yarn: approximately 400g of DK weight yarn. A smooth, plied yarn shows the V-stitch structure clearly. Hook: 4mm. You will also need a tapestry needle, scissors, and a tape measure. A foam blocking mat and rust-proof pins are helpful for the final shaping.

One V-stitch (2 tr, ch 1, 2 tr) measures approximately 3cm wide on a 4mm hook over the V-stitch mesh. Tension is not critical for a shawl, but if your tension is tighter than stated the finished piece will be smaller. Work a swatch if you need a specific size.
V-st: 2 tr, ch 1, 2 tr in same ch sp

The shawl starts at the top centre with a single chain and increases by one V-stitch at each edge on every row. The centre V-stitch is worked into the centre chain space of the previous row each time. The turning chain at the start of each row is ch 4, which counts as 1 tr plus ch 1 and forms the left-hand arm of the first V at the edge. A matching tr is placed at the end of the row to form the right-hand arm of the last V.
Ch 4 (counts as tr + ch 1), 2 tr in 6th ch from hook, ch 1, V-st in same ch, ch 1, 2 tr in same ch, ch 1, tr in same ch, turn. (3 V-sts)
Ch 4 (counts as tr + ch 1), 2 tr in first ch-1 sp, [V-st in ch-1 sp of each V-st across], 2 tr in last ch-1 sp, ch 1, tr in 3rd ch of turning ch, turn. (5 V-sts)
Ch 4 (counts as tr + ch 1), 2 tr in first ch-1 sp (edge V half), [V-st in ch-1 sp of each V-st across], 2 tr in last ch-1 sp, ch 1, tr in 3rd ch of turning ch, turn.
Each row adds 2 V-stitches. Continue until the top edge measures approximately 150cm or you have approximately 50 V-stitches across one row. End with a WS row. Fasten off, leaving a 15cm tail.
Work one round of dc around the entire edge, placing 3 dc at each corner to keep the fabric flat. Fasten off and weave in the tail.

Weave in all ends on the wrong side. Block by soaking in cool water, removing excess moisture in a towel, then pinning to the stated dimensions on a foam mat. Pin the top edge straight and ease the lower point to a sharp angle. Leave to dry completely. Blocking sets the open mesh and straightens the top edge.
Hand wash in cool water with a gentle detergent. Reshape while damp and dry flat. Check the yarn label for fibre-specific guidance. Do not tumble dry.

Once chain spaces feel easy, try the classic prayer shawl. It uses a shell pattern over chain spaces for a denser result. The ripple chevron shawl adds a zigzag line to the same triangle shape. For a firmer fabric, the basketweave wrap uses post stitches in DK weight for a very different texture.
